question: What is the name of the festival observed alongside Karam by unmarried tribal girls in Jharkhand and nearby regions?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jawa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jawa** is a significant cultural and religious festival observed by **unmarried tribal girls** in the state of **Jharkhand** and its neighboring regions.
 
• This festival is celebrated in conjunction with the **Karam festival**, which is one of the most important festivals of the tribal communities in the region, particularly among the **Oraon, Munda, and Santhal tribes**.
 
• The primary focus of the **Jawa festival** is to pray for prosperity, fertility, and better agricultural productivity. It also emphasizes the health and well-being of the family. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• During this festival, the young tribal girls plant **Jawa seeds (barley or paddy)** in a small basket filled with fertile soil. These seeds are then nurtured with care and devotion over a period of **seven to nine days**.
 
• On the day of the festival, the **Jawa plants** are used as offerings during the main ritual performed by the community. The festival is marked by traditional songs, dances, and rituals. Hence, the statement is correct.
 
• The synchronized celebration of **Karam** and **Jawa** highlights the deep connection of tribal communities with nature and their agricultural way of life.
 
• The festival also provides an opportunity for young girls to bond, celebrate their culture, and pray for a prosperous future. Hence, the statement is correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Karam Festival:**

 
 
• The **Karam festival** is one of the most prominent tribal festivals in **Jharkhand** and is dedicated to the worship of the **Karam tree**, which symbolizes fertility, prosperity, and the well-being of the community.
 
• It is celebrated with great enthusiasm by the **Oraon, Munda, and Santhal tribes**. The festival involves traditional rituals, songs, and dances, focusing on the importance of nature in the lives of the tribal people.
 
• The festival is celebrated during the **monsoon season** when the Karam tree is worshipped, and the community seeks blessings for a good harvest.
 
 
 
• **Jawa Festival:**
 
 
• The **Jawa festival** is celebrated alongside the Karam festival by unmarried girls, who plant and nurture **Jawa seeds** (barley or paddy) as a symbolic act of devotion and hope for prosperity.
 
• It provides an opportunity for young girls to showcase their dedication, celebrate their cultural heritage, and pray for a bright future.
 
• The synchronized celebration of Karam and Jawa signifies the deep-rooted connection of tribal communities with **agriculture and nature**.
 
 
 
• **Other Tribal Festivals:**
 
 
• **Sohrai:** This is a harvest festival celebrated by the tribes of Jharkhand to mark the season of reaping crops and is accompanied by rituals and traditional art forms like **Sohrai paintings**.
 
• **Sarhul:** This is a spring festival celebrated by tribal communities to worship trees and nature for their role in sustaining life. It marks the beginning of the **new year** as per the tribal calendar.
 
• **Madai:** This is a festival celebrated by the tribal communities of **Chhattisgarh**, involving traditional rituals, dance, and music to honor their deities and seek blessings.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Tribal Festivals:**

 
 
• Tribal festivals like **Karam** and **Jawa** hold immense cultural and religious importance as they signify the deep connection of tribal communities with **nature and agriculture**.
 
• These festivals also serve as occasions for social bonding, community participation, and the preservation of tribal traditions and heritage.
 
 
 
• **Role of Unmarried Girls in Jawa:**
 
 
• The participation of unmarried girls in the Jawa festival emphasizes their role in nurturing and sustaining life, both symbolically and culturally.
 
• The rituals performed during Jawa not only highlight the importance of agriculture but also reinforce the values of **care, dedication, and hope** for a prosperous future.
